title: Prevent Protocol
author: Virginia Sanchez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t3yeqpw

steps.title: Obtain Ethical and Administrative Approvals
steps.instruction: Secure necessary permissions to begin the study.

substeps.instruction: Request project approval from the Comité Coordinador de Ética de la Investigación Biomédica de Andalucía.
Request collaboration from the educational administration for the selection and contact of educational centers.

steps.title: Select and Recruit Educational Centers
steps.instruction: Identify and recruit a minimum of 10 public ESO educational centers in Western Andalusia based on specific criteria.

substeps.instruction: Filter centers by Socioeconomic and Cultural Index (ISC), selecting 2 centers for each level (low, medium-low, medium, medium-high, and high).
Ensure centers have students enrolled in ESO and a ratio of at least 250 students.
Randomly select 10 centers from the provided administration list.
Assign centers randomly to either the experimental group or the control group.
If RCT/QRCT is not possible due to center refusal, use accessibility sampling with at least 6 centers (3 per condition).

steps.title: Prepare Measurement Instruments
steps.instruction: Systematize the battery of validated instruments to be used for data collection.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the European Bullying Intervention Project Questionnaire for bullying.
Prepare the European Cyberbullying Intervention Project Questionnaire for cyberbullying.
Prepare the Spanish adaptation of the Sexual Harassment Survey (AAUW; 1991) for sexual violence.
Prepare the Spanish adaptation of the CTS-2 (Strauss, 1996) for physical partner violence.
Prepare the Menesini et al. (2010) adaptation for psychological partner violence.
Prepare the Cyberdating_Q-A for online partner violence.
Include validated instruments for socio-emotional factors, peer networks, and teachers, as well as implementation fidelity and satisfaction scales.

steps.title: Design the Psychoeducational Program
steps.instruction: Develop the intervention program based on previous models and explanatory frameworks of adolescent interpersonal violence.

substeps.instruction: Review and introduce contents covering common risk factors across different forms of interpersonal violence.
Determine the number of lessons or modules for students and teachers.
Design support and dissemination materials, including a website.

steps.title: Implement the Intervention
steps.instruction: Execute the program in experimental centers using trained teaching staff.

substeps.instruction: Train the teachers who will implement the program.
Conduct the program during tutoring hours, once per week.
Hold bi-weekly meetings with each center via project team members and support staff.
Use the project website for forums, queries, experience exchange, and lesson evaluation.

steps.title: Execute Data Collection Timeline
steps.instruction: Collect data across multiple time points for both experimental and control groups.

substeps.instruction: Perform five data collections in control centers (the third collection serves as the pretest for the second objective).
Perform three data collections in experimental centers.
Administer the post-test to both experimental and control centers immediately after the program ends.
Perform a follow-up (second post-test) between 3 and 6 months after program completion.

steps.title: Conduct Final Dissemination and Analysis
steps.instruction: Share results with participants and perform statistical analysis of the data.

substeps.instruction: Organize conferences with teachers, students, and families in the centers.
Deliver a scientific-technical report to the centers detailing interpersonal violence and risk factors.
Perform confirmatory factor analysis, longitudinal invariance, and multilevel analysis (student, classroom, and center levels) using SPSS, MPLUS_7, LISREL, and EQS.
Use latent curves to evaluate program efficacy, sustainability, and mediators.
Analyze the impact on both the preventive condition and the population previously involved in violence (identified via pretest).
